class: A question was known to be required only from a star in its name, and a bare 'Required' alert inside it was not read as the site's complaint
symptom: Walmart (careers.walmart.com), Military Service (voluntary disclosure, 71%): 'Have you already left Active Duty ...' was left blank as optional; after Continue the site showed a red 'Required' alert inside the question, and the run pressed Continue three times until the loop guard stopped it for the owner ('the page did not change after three tries').
site: Walmart careers site, 27 October 2026 (saved pages output/Walmart_(USA)_Senior_Network_Engineer/pages/20261027_231617, page_11-12)
root_cause: required_questions finds required questions by an asterisk in a name or label. This question's name (410 characters, ending 'other than “Yes”.') carries none; the site signals 'required' only by an alert inside the question after a failed Continue. page_errors deliberately ignores the bare word 'Required' (it is also a column or field label, e.g. 'Degree Graduate Required'), so the one signal that mattered was filtered out and the question stayed optional.
why_tests_missed: Required-marking tests used starred names and the Workday legend; none had a question without a star that the site flagged only with an inline alert.
fix: inline_required_questions reads an alert whose own words are only 'Required' (or 'This field is required') inside a question's block as the site's word that this question is required and unanswered. required_questions includes it, so the answering pass treats the question as required; page_errors reports it by name ('<question>: Required') so the planner and the owner are told which one. An alert outside any question marks nothing, and a label that merely contains the word is still not an error.
prevention: Take 'required' from every signal the site gives (a star, a legend, an inline alert after a failed press), not from one convention; keep structure (an alert inside a named question) as the evidence, never the bare word.
